title: Who ran it
lede: Two of the best-known executives in their industries, and a senior team that changed around them. Later careers are included only where we found a source.

people.name: Jeffrey Katzenberg
people.text: Aged 69 at launch. Former chairman of Walt Disney Studios and co-founder of DreamWorks; he sold DreamWorks Animation in 2016 and formed the holding company WndrCo, where the idea began as NewTV.[^4][^5] He chose the programming and, by Vulture’s account, gave notes on individual scenes.[^4]
people.later: Signed the Eko settlement statement as “founder and chairman of Quibi” in September 2021.[^21]

people.name: Meg Whitman
people.text: Aged 63 at launch. Former chief executive of eBay and of Hewlett-Packard, recruited by Katzenberg as she left Hewlett Packard Enterprise.[^4][^5] She told Vulture that Quibi was the premium version of a free product, like bottled water.[^4]
people.later: Confirmed as United States ambassador to Kenya in July 2022.[^37]

people.name: Tom Conrad
people.text: Demonstrated Turnstyle at CES in January 2020; Engadget identified him as a founder of Pandora.[^26] He announced AirPlay support in May 2020 with the line that “these days visiting the family room is like a day trip.”[^30]

people.name: Ambereen Toubassy
people.text: Announced the $750 million second round in March 2020: “This round of $750 million gives us tremendous flexibility and the financial wherewithal to build content and technology that consumers embrace.”[^3]

people.name: Janice Min
people.role: Head of Daily Essentials (left before launch)
people.text: The former editor of The Hollywood Reporter oversaw the daily news and lifestyle programming and left after reportedly clashing with Katzenberg over its direction.[^4]

people.name: Tim Connelly
people.text: Led the team that secured the first-year advertising commitments, then “left abruptly,” according to Vulture.[^4]

people.name: Megan Imbres
people.text: Her departure was announced two weeks after launch.[^4]

people.name: Yoni Bloch
people.role: Founder and chief executive of Eko (the plaintiff)
people.text: Met Katzenberg in March 2017 and later sued over Turnstyle. After the settlement he said the result “will help ensure that Eko remains the undisputed leader in interactive storytelling technology.”[^21][^22]
